decisions.reason: Although its standalone visibility was no longer evident by 2020–2021, a small-volume ionization chamber still fits the firm's core dosimetry capabilities, so boundedly rational management would likely retain it while tolerating some uncertainty and overlap.

Because this chamber is close to the firm's established measurement business but may overlap with neighboring products and showed no clear public prominence after launch, management would keep it with a somewhat elevated withdrawal risk.

A standard clinical ionization chamber line sits near the center of the firm's aspiration-defining core business, making continued retention more likely unless internal performance has clearly fallen short.

This relative-dosimetry chamber serves a narrower use case, so it faces more scrutiny if uptake is modest, but its fit with the installed customer base and shared support resources still favors keeping it.

A thimble ionization chamber is a conventional, complementary radiotherapy QA product, and the firm's service capabilities and organizational slack make continued offering more likely than withdrawal.
